payload.title: A large backend release is never killed by the build timeout
payload.description:
Repo: **Papyrus**. Priority 1: every large schema release can hit this on every site.

## What happened (2026-11-14)
Machines on Machines Amplify job 107 (app d260vp72hqglnc, branch main) ran 12:52:25 to 13:22:38 ET, exactly 30 minutes, and ended FAILED with no error in the build log. The backend CloudFormation update (root stack amplify-d260vp72hqglnc-main-branch-6d46e58456) was still UPDATE_IN_PROGRESS server-side: Amplify's default build timeout killed the CDK client (ampx pipeline-deploy) mid-deploy. Papyrus 5.111.0 added the tenant listing index to about 30 tables, the Item language-group index and new models; creating those takes more than 30 minutes.

## Evidence
- Docs (AWS Amplify Hosting user guide, "Troubleshooting build issues", "I want to override a build timeout"): default 30 minutes, override with the `_BUILD_TIMEOUT` environment variable, minimum 5, maximum 120 minutes.
- CloudFormation `AWS::Amplify::App` has no timeout property. `JobConfig` has only `BuildComputeType`; `AWS::Amplify::Branch` has none either. `buildSpec` has no timeout key. The only supported control is the `_BUILD_TIMEOUT` environment variable, which `AWS::Amplify::App.EnvironmentVariables` and `AWS::Amplify::Branch.EnvironmentVariables` accept (CLI equivalents: `aws amplify update-app --environment-variables`, `update-branch --environment-variables`; branch overrides app).
- Our app shell sets it nowhere: `infra/amplify-app-shell/lib/amplify-app-shell.ts` creates `CfnApp "App"` (~line 222, only `jobConfig.buildComputeType` is set, no environmentVariables) and `CfnBranch "Branch"` for main (~line 275, `environmentVariables({...})`). `grep _BUILD_TIMEOUT` finds it only in `packages/papyrus/src/backend-deploy.mjs` (`deployMinutes`: timeout less 10 minutes reserved for the frontend build; default 30), `scripts/test-backend-deploy.mjs`, `docs/cost-accounting.md` and `infra/amplify-app-shell/features/cost-tags.feature`. So our own cost-tag wave logic already knows that a build may have a different timeout, but nothing sets it. Cost-tag waves were an earlier workaround for the same wall (one deploy pass per wave, fitted to the timeout).
- Scope: the AWS docs do not say which phases count. The job 107 wall clock (30m13s from start to end, including clone and setup) matches the whole job, not only the BUILD step, and our `deployMinutes` assumes the same (timeout less 10 minutes). Treat the timeout as covering the whole Amplify job.
- Other sites: no earlier timeout is recorded in docs/site-hosting.md, docs/amplify-cost-check.md, docs/hosting or the board (searched for 30 minutes / timed out / build timeout); the only trace is PPY-75d87d94 ("Note the Amplify build-timeout lesson for schema changes", unwritten) and the cost-tag wave design. The Anth.us rebuild is not recorded as a timeout. Job 107 is the first recorded one. AWS-side caveat: two aws-amplify GitHub issues (amplify-backend #1942 and amplify-hosting) report builds that still timed out with `_BUILD_TIMEOUT` set to 120 or 180, anecdotal and old, so the fix must be verified on a real job.
- Workflow side: `.github/workflows/amplify-deploy.yml` waits `timeout-minutes` (default 60) and the job has `timeout-minutes: 90`; both already exceed 30 and a 120-minute build needs the wait raised above 120 (or the job fails while Amplify still runs).
- GSI ledger (`scripts/lib/gsi-ledger.ts`, `features_backend/gsi-ledger.feature`, docs/releasing.md): limits one new index per table per release but not the NUMBER of tables with a new index per release (`compareLedgers` collects all tables into `releaseOrder` group 1). Job 107 shows that count matters. DynamoDB backfills indexes of different tables concurrently, but CloudFormation's nested-stack concurrency and per-table backfill make total time depend on both table size and count; we have one measurement only (about 30 tables did not fit in 30 minutes).

## Fix
Primary (proper, infrastructure as code): set `_BUILD_TIMEOUT` in the app shell on the `CfnApp` (all branches) as an `environmentVariables` entry, value from a new site config key `cms.buildTimeoutMinutes` (integer 5 to 120, default 120 for sites that deploy their backend in the build), validated in `site-config.ts` next to `buildComputeType`, applied by the pipeline-run app-shell deploy (nothing by hand). `deployMinutes` then reads the same value, so cost-tag waves and any release budget use the real timeout. Raise the `amplify-deploy.yml` wait default and job timeout above the build timeout.
Second (still needed, because the ceiling is 120): a release budget in the GSI ledger. The check fails when a release adds more index creations (tables with a new index, with table sizes where known) than fit the build timeout, computed from a measured seconds-per-index-creation figure recorded in the repo (first data point: job 107; later builds append measured times from the CloudFormation events). It prints which indexes go in release 1, 2, 3, as it does for the one-per-table rule.

## Acceptance (Gherkin)
```gherkin
Feature: A large backend release is never killed by the build timeout

  Scenario: The app shell sets the build timeout in infrastructure as code
    Given a site config with cms.buildTimeoutMinutes 120
    When the app shell template is synthesized
    Then the Amplify app has an environment variable _BUILD_TIMEOUT with value "120"
    And no other variable or script sets it

  Scenario: The timeout defaults to the maximum for a site that deploys its backend in the build
    Given a site config that does not set cms.buildTimeoutMinutes
    When the app shell template is synthesized
    Then the Amplify app has _BUILD_TIMEOUT "120"

  Scenario: A value outside Amplify's range is refused
    Given a site config with cms.buildTimeoutMinutes 121 or 4
    When the site config is validated
    Then validation fails saying the range is 5 to 120 minutes

  Scenario: The deploy passes use the configured timeout
    Given _BUILD_TIMEOUT is "120" in the build environment
    When papyrus-infra backend-deploy computes its time
    Then it has 110 minutes for deploying

  Scenario: The deploy workflow waits longer than the build can run
    Given a build timeout of 120 minutes
    When amplify-deploy starts the job
    Then its wait and its own job timeout are more than 120 minutes

  Scenario: A release that adds too many index creations fails CI
    Given a change that adds one new index to each of 40 tables
    And the measured time per index creation makes that more than the build timeout less 10 minutes
    When CI runs the GSI ledger check
    Then the check fails saying how many index creations fit one release
    And it lists which indexes belong in release 1, 2 and 3

  Scenario: A release that fits the budget passes
    Given a change that adds one new index to each of 5 tables
    When CI runs the GSI ledger check
    Then the check passes and prints its estimated deploy minutes

  Scenario: The measured time is recorded
    Given a release whose backend update finished
    Then its CloudFormation duration and index creation count are appended to the ledger's measurements

  Scenario: A real deploy longer than 30 minutes completes
    Given the app shell deployed with the timeout set
    When an Amplify job on a site runs a backend update that takes 35 minutes
    Then the job ends SUCCEED and is not stopped at 30 minutes
```
